design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — dental_ppo_member_services task 0 (env_0070), rework round 3. Frozen time 2026-02-24 11:20:00 PST.

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0: one prerequisite problem, factor counts [4, 6]. The initial-wait reprocessing takes 6 factors, the member's estimate request 4.

[Scope] Claimed here: dental_ext_initial_wait_reprocess -> reprocess_wait_denial_e5c18a2f (agent) and dental_ext_estimate_request -> submit_estimate_request_d87add4f (owner=user). Task 1 claims the claim appeal, the new-plan-wait, grace-period and prior-level reprocessing rules. The member's estimate request is the member's own act (the base rule lets the member request a pre-treatment estimate).

[Why a good test] Lorraine Bassett asks only for a new estimate for the custom abutment (D6057) on tooth 19, the treatment plan her in-network dentist already sent in January (estimate PTE71-26011406, ESTIMATE_WAITING_PERIOD). The estimate rule waits until her most recently decided claim line that was denied for the waiting period counted from the coverage effective date, a waiting period her earlier DHMO enrollment has already served, has been reprocessed: the 2026-01-21 implant on tooth 19 (claim D71-260127-6590, out-of-network oral surgeon) stands DENIED_WAITING_PERIOD. Her DentalCare DHMO 315 ran 2022-01-01 to 2025-02-28, the day before her Premier 2000 group coverage began on 2025-03-01, and tooth 19 was extracted under that DHMO on 2024-09-17. The implant correction must be booked first because its payment uses up the rest of her 2026 annual maximum and 50.00 of her rollover balance, which caps the estimate.

[Problem tree] root dental_ext_estimate_request (user) -> dental_ext_initial_wait_reprocess, value_input, gate room, state form, affirmative sentence "An estimate's figures are worked out only after the person's most recently decided claim line that was denied for the waiting period counted from the coverage effective date, a waiting period the person's earlier DHMO enrollment has already served, has been reprocessed." Only the initial-wait rule rebooks such a line (the new-plan-wait rule covers lines after a plan change; this enrollment never changed). Skipping the correction gives 224.0 instead of 260.0.

[Seed realism and ledgers] Lorraine is an active employee of Calloway Freight Systems (group contract G-7136650, Cascade Group Dental & Vision 20-49, Premier 2000 offered, rates 50.25 / 97.60 / 104.55 / 158.10, rate guarantee to 2026-12-31). She was added as a late entrant effective 2025-03-01 (reported 2025-02-11). The group list-bill account bills the contract rate times the census by tier: the March 2025 invoice issued 2025-01-30 billed the January census (11/4/3/5 = 2047.30), a supplementary invoice of 50.25 on 2025-02-12 added her March month, and every invoice from April 2025 bills 12/4/3/5 = 2097.55; remittances paid each month through February 2026, the March 2026 invoice is open (balance 2097.55). Her DHMO was funded by an individual direct-bill account: 38 monthly invoices of 15.40 (DHMO 315 member_only premium) from January 2022 to February 2025, each paid by card (the first as binder), closed 2025-03-06 on her confirmed closure request of 2025-03-04. She also has coverage through a part-time employer (Evergreen Dental Mutual), on file since 2019, which pays first under the longer-coverage rule; Premier coordinates by standard coordination of benefits. 2025 history: a 2025-04-08 in-network exam and cleaning (preventive, exempt from Premier's maximum) and a 2025-10-14 filling after the 6-month basic wait (90.00 to the maximum, 50.00 deductible), so 2025 maximum used was 90.00 and the 350.00 rollover credit was posted on 2026-01-01. 2026 history: two in-network root canals (basic, waits served) on 2026-01-06 and 2026-01-08, each paid 450.00 under standard coordination, the first taking the 50.00 deductible; 2026 maximum used 900.00.

[Computation 1, step 20, initial-wait reprocessing, expected 250.0] credit 38 months (DHMO 2022-01..2025-02, both months counted) against the 12-month late-entrant major wait; clause credit 38 months (the services of her earlier DHMO enrollment, the one that ended the day before coverage, record the extraction of tooth 19 on the line's extraction date) added to 10 months of enrollment against the 12-month clause; out-of-network major 50%; allowance 2300.00 (billed below the 2400.00 allowed); deductible 0.00; normal (2300.00 - 0.00) x 50% = 1150.00; standard coordination limit 2400.00 - 900.00 = 1500.00 not binding; rollover plan: limit 1100.00 + 350.00 = 1450.00, so 1150.00 is paid, 50.00 of it from rollover; patient share 2300.00 - 1150.00 - 900.00 = 250.00. Factor baselines: dhmo months 0 -> 1400.0; clause months 0 -> 1400.0; in-network 60% -> 20.0; allowed 2400.00 -> 200.0; remaining maximum only -> 300.0; no primary credit -> 1150.0; all baselines -> 2300.0.

[Computation 2, step 22, estimate request, expected 260.0] after the correction: remaining 2026 maximum 0.00, rollover balance 300.00; estimate facts from PTE71-26011406 (D6057, tooth 19, in_network_ppo, fee 560.00, recorded allowance 600.00); class major (the implant decision); extraction date 2024-09-17 from her latest tooth-19 claim line, recorded among her earlier DHMO enrollment's services; the implant interval counts only same-code lines on the tooth position, so the D6010 body booked by the initial-wait correction does not limit the D6057 abutment; allowance 560.00 (lesser of fee and recorded allowance); deductible 0.00; credits 38/38 months serve the wait and the clause on the 2026-02-24 issue date (11 months enrolled); in-network major 60%: 336.00, limited by the rollover tier to 0.00 + 300.00 = 300.00; patient cost 560.00 - 300.00 = 260.00; valid through 2027-02-24 (365 days). Factor baselines: estimate credit 0 -> 560.0; clause credit 0 -> 560.0; out-of-network 50% -> 280.0 (280.00 under the 300.00 limit); remaining maximum only -> 560.0; all baselines -> 560.0.

[Stamps and near misses] The denied implant line carries no allowance-used stamp; the tier taken (billed below allowed) is read by comparing 2300.00 with 2400.00. The January estimate's recorded allowance (600.00) is not the figure used (560.00). Near misses: the 2026-01-21 line is the only DENIED_WAITING_PERIOD line; the 2025 rollover credit is the only credit row; the DHMO cleaning of 2024-03-12 is not an extraction; the employer's rows belong to the group and are not the person's.

[Persona] Lorraine raises only the new estimate; she agrees to any correction only when the representative raises it, and gives the other-coverage name only when asked.


[Round 3] D1: every DHMO read is the person's own: the earlier DHMO enrollment is matched by name and date of birth and must have ended the day before coverage, and DHMO services are read only under that enrollment's id (a household member's DHMO extraction of the same tooth, or the person's older DHMO enrollment, is not read; probes in the worklog). T0-G1: the estimate rule declares, by an overwrite of the base interval sentence scoped to estimates under it, that implant services of the same kind share a procedure code, as carriers limit the implant body and the abutment separately; after the initial-wait correction books the D6010 body on tooth 19 the D6057 estimate is therefore not frequency-limited by the in-force rules. T0-G2: the frequency and clause proof lines now describe the world at the estimate's handling time. D3: the pediatric crossing now has one reading (share limited first, plan payment = allowance less the limited share); no pediatric person here.

[Round 6, seed only] src-2: the in-network lines (2025-04-08 exam and cleaning, 2025-10-14 filling, the January root canals) and the January estimate name the active Cascade PPO Participating Dentist Agreement of Helen M. Ashford, DDS at Ashford Family Dental PLLC (general dentist, private practice, WA; complete credentialing application received 2014-11-10, approved 2015-01-20, in network from 2015-02-01, the first of the month after approval; recredentialed every 36 months, most recently on 2024-01-18, before the 2024-01-20 due date, so the next due date is 2027-01-18; liability 1,000,000 / 3,000,000); the practice holds no Premier agreement, so the recorded in_network_ppo is the network the agreements give. Her DHMO 315 enrollment is assigned to Marcus T. Ilves, DDS of Proctor District Family Dentistry under an active Cascade DHMO Primary Care Dentist Agreement (application 2015-05-26, approved after site review 2015-08-03, in network from 2015-09-01; recredentialed most recently on 2024-07-29, due 2027-07-29), and both DHMO services name it. Four gold look-ups read these agreements. src-3: each DHMO visit now carries the DHMO 315 office visit copay of 5.00 with its procedure copay (cleaning 10.00 + 5.00 = 15.00; surgical extraction 85.00 + 5.00 = 90.00). No scored value moved; the gold writes shifted four steps later because of the added reads.

[Round 7, seed only] E1: each provider agreement now records its original credentialing application date and the effective date the approval produced (first of the month after the original decision); the credentialing decision date, recredential due date, licence and liability fields are the ones the latest recredentialing refreshed, the only fields that event writes. Each practice profile was opened before its first application.
user_scenario: You are Lorraine Bassett, a 42-year-old dispatch coordinator at Calloway Freight Systems in Tacoma, Washington: organized, polite and a little impatient with jargon. You are calling Cascade Mutual Dental & Vision about the dental PPO you have through work. Your member ID is CM71620934, your date of birth is 1983-08-14 and your ZIP code is 98404; give them when asked. Your lower-left back tooth (tooth 19) was pulled in 2024 while you were on Cascade's DentalCare DHMO, which you had for about three years until you joined your employer's PPO in March 2025 with no break in between. An oral surgeon placed an implant there in January, and your regular dentist, Ashford Family Dental, now wants to put the custom abutment on it, the same treatment plan they sent in January. The estimate you got back in January said a waiting period applied and the plan would pay nothing. You want a new estimate for that abutment today, and you will submit the estimate request yourself during the call if the representative tells you exactly what to enter. You also have dental coverage through a part-time job, Evergreen Dental Mutual, which pays first; mention it only if asked. You do not know any dollar figures or plan rules and do not guess them. If the representative says something on your claims has to be corrected or reprocessed before the estimate, you tell them that's fine and to go ahead. When you have the new estimate reference you thank them and end the call.

base_preconditions.condition: The estimate is tested against the 12-month late-entrant major wait counted from 2025-03-01, shortened by the credit the extended rule states.

At the estimate's handling time the initial-wait correction has booked the corrected D6010 implant-body decision on tooth 19 (date of service 2026-01-21). Under the estimate rule's declared frequency treatment the implant interval counts only earlier paid or reprocessed lines with the same procedure code on the same tooth position; no D6057 abutment on tooth 19 has ever been paid or reprocessed, so no interval limit applies, and implant services carry no age limit.

The extraction date recorded on her most recently decided tooth-19 claim line (2024-09-17) is before the coverage effective date; the 12-month clause applies, shortened by the clause credit the extended rule states (the services of her DHMO 315 enrollment, which ended the day before her PPO coverage, record that extraction).
An estimate may be issued only while the enrollment is active.

edges.policy_source: An estimate's figures are worked out only after the person's most recently decided claim line that was denied for the waiting period counted from the coverage effective date, a waiting period the person's earlier DHMO enrollment has already served, has been reprocessed.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The 2026-01-21 implant on tooth 19 (claim D71-260127-6590) still stands DENIED_WAITING_PERIOD, although the DentalCare DHMO that ended 2025-02-28 gives 38 months against the 12-month wait.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: One edge only: the implant correction must precede the estimate. There is no parallel prerequisite to reorder.
